trust_decision.summary: Is the pack-entry target path refused when it contains a '..' segment, both at pack build time and at install time before it is turned into a File and written? Decided twice: in PackFile's constructor (izpack-api) and again in UnpackerBase.unpack before createDirectory/extract.

landing_point.why: The advisory names UnpackerBase; here the pack-supplied target path is variable-expanded and converted straight to a File that is later created and written, with no validation.

fix_sites.entry_point: installer runtime: IUnpacker.run()/unpack() -> UnpackerBase.unpack(PackFile,...) from the GUI, console and automated InstallPanel
public data API: PackInfo.addFile() and new PackFile(...)/new XPackFile(...), reached by the izpack-compiler CLI and by external tooling
PackFile(File baseDir, File src, String target, ...) constructors via FileUtil.getRelativeFileName

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The PackFile constructor is a low-level builder used by the trusted compiler/API to produce the pack, so its target is not attacker-controlled; the report is only about unpacking.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Absolute target paths that legitimately land outside the install directory (e.g. /etc, ProgramData, shared dirs) must keep working; the published fix only logs an audit warning for them and its own test asserts they stay allowed (fix.diff:1443-1447).

O6_input_shapes: target with a trailing '/', stripped at PackFile.java:178-181
variable-expanded target checked after IoHelper.translatePath (UnpackerBase.java:623, IoHelper.java:303-315)
absolute path outside the install root: allowed and merely audited

O7_producer.where: izpack-api/src/main/java/com/izforge/izpack/api/data/PackFile.java:43-60 (PackFile is Serializable, targetPath travels through packs.info and is deserialized at izpack-installer/src/main/java/com/izforge/izpack/installer/unpacker/UnpackerBase.java:311-314); the runtime check never visits the producer, so the published fix also re-validates in the constructor

O8_uncovered_routes.route: overrideRenameTo rename target: an existing target file is renamed to a GlobPatternMapper result built from the pack's overrideRenameTo attribute, so '../../..' escapes the install directory
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: overrideRenameTo is an author-supplied rename pattern applied to a file that already exists, not a pack target path
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file, ~700 lines from the landing point; the attribute is read in another module at izpack-compiler/src/main/java/com/izforge/izpack/compiler/CompilerConfig.java:3427-3438

O8_uncovered_routes.route: parsable target path: IoHelper.translatePath(parsableFile.getPath()) is rewritten in place by ScriptParser with no traversal validation
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: a parsable only rewrites a file that already exists (UnpackerBase.java:1370), so it cannot create files outside the install directory
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: separate class in the same package; the path comes from the compiler's <parsable targetfile> handling (izpack-compiler/src/main/java/com/izforge/izpack/compiler/CompilerConfig.java:1431-1465)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a second target-path check inside getTarget(), which also creates the blockable temp file next to the target
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: every FileUnpacker subclass funnels its write through getTarget, so a maintainer fixing a bypass would naturally guard it there too

O8b_injection_room.sibling: validate the parsable path before creating the temp file and renaming it back
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: same install-time variable substitution and the same class of attacker-chosen path in the same module

O8b_injection_room.sibling: validate paths read back from the install log before deleting
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the uninstaller consumes paths recorded from pack entries across a serialization boundary, an obvious place to repeat the same check

O9_family: path traversal / zip-slip in archive extraction (CWE-22)

O10_build.toolchain: Maven multi-module build (pom.xml, mvnw wrapper), maven.compiler.release=11 (pom.xml:50), 19 modules incl. a native C++ parent
O10_build.project_tests: JUnit: izpack-installer/src/test/java/com/izforge/izpack/installer/unpacker/{AbstractFileUnpackerTest,DefaultFileUnpackerTest,LooseFileUnpackerTest,Pack200FileUnpackerTest,ScriptParserTest}.java plus izpack-test integration tests (MultiVolumeUnpackerTest); the fix's new PackFileTest and UnpackerBaseTest do not exist at the pinned commit

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Normalize/canonicalize the target in UnpackerBase.unpack and reject anything not under installData.getInstallPath(), fixing only the reported sink and breaking legitimate out-of-root installs.

out_of_scope_notes: izpack-uninstaller/src/main/java/com/izforge/izpack/uninstaller/Destroyer.java:190-203 deletes paths read back from the install log without validation; that is a deletion sink, outside this advisory's write property, so it was not pursued.

izpack-installer/src/main/java/com/izforge/izpack/installer/container/provider/AbstractInstallDataProvider.java:19-20 gains only unused java.nio.file imports in the published fix; no behavioural change.
izpack-native-parent holds C++ sources that cannot be built in this environment; they are unrelated to this path handling.
unverified: repo_mb not measured (shell disabled, no du).
O8 present_in_latest unknown: the inputs give no latest code for this repo, so latest_where is 'none'.
Whether the FileUtil.getRelativeFileName rewrite (canonical strings -> Path.relativize) is security-relevant or incidental refactoring in the same commit.
O7 check_calls_producer is false for the runtime check, but the published fix also adds the same check to the constructor that produces the state before serialization.
